home.empty.heading: Nothing in this game yet
home.empty.sentence: Maestro holds what your game is made of: its missions, its places, its classes, whatever your game calls them, how they connect, and the writing about them. You do not type any of it in here. Your agent writes it, and you read it, judge it and correct it.
home.empty.key: Make a key for this game
home.empty.step1: , and give it to your agent. The command to paste is on that screen.
home.empty.step2: Ask your agent to read the Maestro guide for this game.
home.empty.step3: Then ask it to start. Something like this:
home.empty.prompt: Read the Maestro skill for {game}, then declare the kinds of things this game is made of and add the first ten of them.
content.empty.heading: This game has not said what it is made of
content.empty.sentence: Every game names its own entities: missions, places and classes in one, drivers, cars and circuits in another. Yours has named none yet.
connections.empty.heading: Nothing connects to anything yet
connections.empty.sentence: A connection is a kind of link between two things: a mission happens in a place, a mission needs another one first, a reward unlocks a class.
writing.empty.heading: Nothing written yet
writing.empty.sentence: This is where the words go: the lore of a place, the brief for a mission, the lines a character says. Every piece keeps its older versions.
overviews.empty.heading: Nothing saved to look at yet
overviews.empty.sentence: An overview is a saved way of seeing part of this game: how its missions unlock each other, where its places sit, what happens in what order.
overviews.empty.compose: You can put a simple one together here. An agent writes the ones that ask a harder question.
overviews.empty.viewer: You can read this game but not change it, so somebody with an editor's or a manager's role saves these.

settings.addressWarning: Changing the address breaks every link into this game.
settings.notYours.heading: Only a game manager can change these
settings.notYours.sentence: A game's name and address are its managers' to change, because changing the address breaks every link into the game for everybody in it.
settings.member.title: What they may do
settings.noMembers.heading: Only you
settings.noMembers.sentence: Nobody else can open this game. An invitation above puts somebody in it, at the role you choose.
settings.noInvites.heading: Nobody is waiting
settings.noInvites.sentence: No invitation into this game is outstanding. One appears here from the moment you create it until the person uses it or you revoke it.
settings.notManager.heading: Only a game manager can change who is here
settings.notManager.sentence: You can see who is in this game and what they may do. Inviting somebody, changing a role or removing a member is a manager's.
settings.lastManager: This game must keep at least one manager. Make somebody else one first.
settings.cannotChangeYourself: This is your own membership. Another manager changes it, so nobody can take their own way into a game away by accident.
settings.token.next: Then tell your agent to start. Its own first call fetches Maestro's instructions — the metamodel, the tools and three worked games — so you do not have to teach it any of that.
settings.token.once: Copy this now. This is the only time this token is shown; if it is lost, create another and revoke this one.
settings.keys.yours: These are your own tokens. Everybody in this game has their own, and only the person who created one can retire it.
settings.keys.every: You manage this game, so this is every token in it, whoever created it — and you can retire any of them.
settings.noKeys.heading: No tokens yet
settings.noKeys.sentence: A token is how an agent reaches this game. Every agent, and every machine an agent runs on, gets its own, so one can be revoked without stopping the rest.
settings.noMint.heading: Only an editor or a game manager can create a token
settings.noMint.sentence: A token carries whatever access this game grants, so it is not a viewer's to hand out. You can still see which tokens exist and revoke one.
settings.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.
admin.noInvites.heading: Nobody is waiting
admin.noInvites.sentence: No invitation is outstanding. One appears here from the moment you create it until the person uses it or you revoke it.
admin.noUsers.heading: Nobody but you
admin.noUsers.sentence: This instance has one account, yours. An invitation above is how a second one is made.
admin.edit.title: Edit this account
admin.lastAdmin: This instance must keep at least one administrator. Make somebody else one first.
admin.cannotDemoteYourself: You are signed in as an administrator. Taking it away here would lock you out of this page, so another administrator does it for you.

checks.truncated.results: The run stopped at its result limit, so there may be more than these.
checks.truncated.depth: The walk stopped at its depth bound, so something further away may exist and this run did not look.
checks.undeclared.head: This game has not said what its connections do
checks.undeclared.body: An analysis walks edges by what they mean, not by what they are called. Until a relation type declares that, there is nothing to follow — and an engine with nothing to follow would answer that nothing is wrong, which is the one answer it must never give.
checks.routes.none: No routes are written yet. An agent writes one; nothing on this page does.

view.removed: This view has been deleted. What is on screen is the last answer it gave.
view.tooNarrow: This window is too narrow to draw the picture, so this view is shown as its table below. The table is the same answer. Arranging the picture is off until the window is wider.

admin.accounts.about: Everybody who can sign in to this instance. An account's address is how they sign in and their name is what everybody else sees; both are yours to correct. An administrator can do everything on this page — administering is about this Maestro, never about one game's content.

settings.people.about: Everybody who can open this game, and what each of them may do. A viewer reads it, an editor writes its content, and a manager also renames the game, invites people and changes what they may do. Administering this instance is a separate thing and grants none of this.
settings.invite.about: The link is shown once, here. Nothing is sent anywhere: this instance delivers no email, so you pass it on yourself.
settings.agents.about: Nothing on these screens writes a game's content. An agent does, over MCP, using a token that opens this game and no other.

games.empty.sentence: Name the game you are working on, and this becomes the place its design lives: every mission, place and character, what a player has to do before each one is available to them, and the lore that goes with it. You will be able to see it drawn, ask it what no player can reach, and hand the whole thing to your agents to fill in and keep straight.
